pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: DeepSeek compatibility is broadened in two ways: OpenAI-provider configurations whose base URL mentions DeepSeek are directed to the standard OpenAI client before Azure detection, and both provider handlers now classify `deepseek-r1` model identifiers as DeepSeek reasoner models. The accompanying changeset describes this as an Azure DeepSeek fix.

behavior_changes.description: When an OpenAI-provider base URL contains both `deepseek` and `azure.com`, client selection changes from `AzureOpenAI` to the standard `OpenAI` client because the DeepSeek condition now takes precedence over the Azure condition.
evidence: The new DeepSeek URL branch constructs `OpenAI`, while Azure client construction is now in the following `else if` branch.
The changeset identifies Azure DeepSeek usage as the intended fix.

citations.quoted_text: Fixed to be able to use DeepSeek in Azure.

behavior_changes.description: Both the dedicated DeepSeek handler and the generic OpenAI handler now classify model identifiers containing `deepseek-r1` as reasoner models, placing those models on the same existing reasoner-specific processing path as `deepseek-reasoner`.
evidence: Each handler expands its reasoner-model predicate to include `deepseek-r1`.

important_symbols.reason: This is the primary compatibility change: it determines whether a configured endpoint is accessed through the standard OpenAI SDK client or the Azure-specific client.
It expands reasoner-model recognition for DeepSeek R1 when DeepSeek is configured through the generic OpenAI provider.
It applies the same DeepSeek R1 classification change to the dedicated DeepSeek provider, so the two provider paths should remain behaviorally consistent.

investigation_hints.description: Trace construction of `OpenAiHandler` and the sources of `openAiBaseUrl`, `openAiApiKey`, and model configuration to determine which provider configurations can enter the new client-selection branch.
Inspect every use of `isDeepseekReasoner` below the shown diff to establish the exact message conversion, streaming, and response-normalization behavior newly applied to DeepSeek R1.
Compare the OpenAI and AzureOpenAI SDK request shapes expected by Azure-hosted DeepSeek deployments, including endpoint paths, API versions, authentication, and streaming event formats.

local_risks.description: Client selection is based on an unanchored substring anywhere in the configured URL. A URL that mentions `deepseek` but still requires Azure-specific SDK semantics will be forced to the standard OpenAI client, potentially making that provider configuration unusable.

Reasoner-model detection remains case-sensitive and uses an unanchored substring. Differently cased R1 identifiers may miss reasoner handling, while identifiers that merely contain the token may receive that handling unintentionally.
